title: bfs + ugrep Native Tool Replacement for Glob/Grep (v2.1.117)
description: In v2.1.117, Claude Code replaced the Glob and Grep built-in tools with embedded `bfs` (breadth-first search, faster than find) and `ugrep` (parallel grep, faster than ripgrep in many cases) on macOS and Linux. Standard npm and native builds are affected. Windows builds are unchanged. No configuration required — automatic at the tool invocation layer. Expected result: Glob and Grep operations are faster without any additional round-trip overhead. Important behavioral note: ugrep is compatible with ripgrep syntax but has edge-case differences in regex handling — any custom Grep patterns relying on ripgrep-specific extensions should be validated.
redundancy_check: NOVEL — no existing registry entry for native tool backend optimization. Glob and Grep were previously ripgrep-based. This is an automatic upgrade requiring awareness for regex compatibility.
preliminary_notes: Score likely 70-80. Automatic, no config, high relevance (Glob/Grep are core tools used in every session). Potential edge case: ugrep regex compatibility with ripgrep patterns. Action: validate common Grep patterns work identically with ugrep backend.

evaluation.reasoning: Automatic backend replacement at zero config cost — pure performance improvement to core tools used in every session. Integration complexity is 100 (Anthropic ships it, nothing to do). Token efficiency is neutral (50): faster grep doesn't reduce token count, only latency. Capability expansion (40): performance improvement and regex compatibility awareness, not a new capability. Maintenance (90): Anthropic-managed backend. Community validation (100): official release. Integration action: registry update documenting the backend change and behavioral note about ugrep edge-case regex differences vs ripgrep (e.g., certain lookaheads or PCRE extensions may behave differently). No workflow changes required — awareness documentation only.
